story.score_reason: Regenerative ag strategy, abstract, not local

carousel.cover_headline:
Only **15%** of Farmland
Is Grown Regeneratively.
Who Fills the Gap?

slides.label: THE GLOBAL PICTURE
slides.headline: Regenerative farming covers just **15%** of global cropland today.
slides.insight: The target is at least 40%. The gap is enormous.

slides.label: THE REAL BARRIER
slides.headline: The business case for farmers doesn't add up yet.
slides.insight: Current incentives don't cover the cost of switching to regenerative methods.

slides.label: THE COST OF DOING NOTHING
slides.headline: Extreme weather costs EU farms **€28.3 billion** every year.
slides.insight: And those losses are expected to rise. The old system is fragile.

slides.label: WHY WE EXIST
slides.headline: If the system won't build it easily, someone must start anyway.
slides.insight: That's why we're building from bare land — and sharing every step.

slides.label: TRY THIS WEEK
slides.headline: Find one local farm or market near you.
slides.insight: Buying local, even once, supports farmers doing things differently.

sources: World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD) / One Planet Business for Biodiversity (OP2B), report by Schuttelaar & Partners and Deloitte, 2026 (reported by WBCSD)
carousel.caption:
Only 15% of farmland is grown regeneratively. Who fills the gap?

A 2026 report found that extreme weather already costs EU farms €28.3 billion a year — and losses are rising. The switch to regenerative farming makes sense, but the numbers don't yet work for most farmers. Someone has to start building anyway.

That's exactly why The Human Fuel exists: to show, honestly, what it takes to grow food that's good for people, soil and community — from bare land up.

Are you seeing more farmers in Malaysia move toward natural growing? Tell us below.

Sources: WBCSD / OP2B, report by Schuttelaar & Partners and Deloitte, 2026 (WBCSD)
